news.title: Dark Matter收购House Numbers扩展AI布局
news.snippet: [Dark Matter收购House Numbers，加速AI战略扩张，或将影响零售、批发等行业。]
news.raw_snippet:
That shift could have implications across retail, wholesale, and correspondent lending operations, particularly for lenders managing large pipelines and seeking to reduce the labor required to move loans from application to funding.

It also places greater importance on how well AI capabilities integrate with existing systems. A tool that automates one task may deliver limited savings if employees still have to transfer information between platforms or manually initiate the next step. [...] The acquisition comes as mortgage technology providers face increasing pressure to demonstrate that AI investments produce measurable operating improvements.

For lenders, the potential savings extend beyond automating individual tasks. Repeated document requests, unresolved conditions, verification delays, and manual handoffs can add time and expense throughout the origination process. [...] Dark Matter CEO Vikas Rao said acquiring House Numbers would accelerate the company's ability to deliver AI capabilities without having to develop the technology internally.

“We’re AI-forward, and we’re disciplined about what we build and what we buy,” Rao said. “House Numbers had already done the incredible work of running AI agents in live production for home lenders.”

The Hong Kong plan follows the Asia-focused lender’s announcement in July that it would hire more than 100 artificial intelligence specialists at an AI ​centre in rival financial hub Singapore.

The investment in AI transformation comes as banks globally cut staff due to AI-driven overhauls, with lenders such as Citi, ⁠Standard Chartered, and Barclays unveiling plans this ⁠year to cut thousands of jobs. [...] The bank ‌aims to launch the institute in the first quarter of 2027, Chief Executive Georges Elhedery said at Hong Kong’s Fintech Week event on Monday.

The AI unit will work with Hong Kong University of Science and Technology as its anchor academic partner, Elhedery said, though he did ‌not ​disclose headcount details.

He added the bank would move ⁠the centre to Hong Kong’s Northern ⁠Metropolis — a mega project bordering mainland China — as soon as its site there was ready. [...] Around 80% of all banks ​in Hong Kong are already adopting AI or generative AI, Eddie Yue, chief executive ​of Hong Kong’s de facto central bank, told the conference.

HSBC’s Elhedery ‌added that HSBC — one of Hong Kong’s largest private-sector employers with 28,000 local staff — was rolling out AI training for its entire global workforce of roughly 200,000 people.
